All eight new blocks are settled and recorded (SCN-014 through SCN-021). Before I re-propose building, two small **edge situations** on the new blocks that I'd confirm in words (no visual change):

- **Importing an empty or non-bookmark HTML file:** it should simply report *"Imported 0"* and change nothing, rather than erroring. And **exporting when you have no bookmarks** produces a valid (empty) bookmarks file. Agree?
- **Deleting the last item in the current page/view** returns you to a valid page (or the friendly empty state) rather than a blank gap. Agree?

Assuming those are fine, here's the **complete scope** now settled for this build — everything from before, plus:

- **Permanent delete** (guarded, separate from Archive) and **editing the address** itself (validated, unique).
- **Bulk selection** — including "all matching the current search/view" — to tag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete together, with selection that clears only when items leave view.
- **Live saved collections** (search + tags), as chips under the tabs.
- **Preservation:** a private, self-contained **local copy** (the **PDF itself** for PDFs), optional **auto-capture**, and a clearly-flagged **public Internet Archive** copy; graceful failure.
- **Import/export** the standard browser-bookmarks file (titles, tags, dates), skipping duplicates.
- **Settings:** default sort, auto local copy, **text size**, **items-per-page** with Previous/Next paging.
- **Real favicon** with fallback, and a **preview image where available**.
- Clean **wrapping** of long titles/notes and many tags is in scope.

Recorded as **outside** this build: a full backup/restore (notes, states, settings, collections, copies), an explicit "refresh details from page," and performance tuning for very large collections. The **local-copy capture, Internet Archive, favicon and preview** rely on external services — real in the build, simulated in this prototype.

**Shall I now start building this full scope for real?** I won't switch to implementation without your explicit go-ahead.
